districts.name: Shibuya
districts.fact: Shibuya Crossing is the busiest pedestrian crossing in the world — up to 3,000 people cross at once! The Hachiko statue nearby is a famous meeting spot.
districts.tips: Visit at night when the neon is brightest. The Starbucks overlooking the crossing is worth the wait.

districts.name: Akihabara
districts.fact: Akihabara is Tokyo's electric town — anime, manga, retro games, and electronics. The Radio Kaikan building has 10 floors of otaku culture.
districts.tips: Check out the retro game shops in the back streets. Super Potato on the main street has classic games.

districts.name: Asakusa
districts.fact: Senso-ji is Tokyo's oldest temple (founded 645 AD). The Thunder Gate (Kaminarimon) with the giant red lantern is the iconic entrance.
districts.tips: Go early morning to avoid crowds. Try freshly made ningyo-yaki (little doll cakes) from the street stalls.

districts.name: Shinjuku
districts.fact: Shinjuku has the busiest train station in the world — 3.6 million passengers daily! The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building has a free observation deck.
districts.tips: The free observatory on the 45th floor of the government building is open until 11pm. Best sunset view in Tokyo.

districts.name: Harajuku
districts.fact: Harajuku is the center of Japanese youth culture and fashion. Takeshita Street is packed with quirky shops, crepe stands, and cosplay.
districts.tips: Try a rainbow crepe from Takeshita Street. Visit on Sunday to see the best street fashion.

districts.name: Ueno Park
districts.fact: Ueno Park has 9 museums, a zoo, and a temple — all in one massive park. The pandas at Ueno Zoo are a national treasure.
districts.tips: The Tokyo National Museum has the largest collection of Japanese art in the world. Allow 2-3 hours.

districts.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
districts.fact: Tsukiji was the world's largest fish market (now moved to Toyosu). The outer market still has 400+ shops selling fresh seafood, knives, and street food.
districts.tips: Go hungry. Try the fresh uni (sea urchin), tamago (egg omelet), and grilled scallops. Cash only at most stalls.

food.name: Ramen
food.description: Rich broth, fresh noodles, sliced pork. Try tonkotsu (pork bone) or shoyu (soy sauce) base.

food.name: Sushi
food.description: Fresh fish over vinegared rice. Conveyor belt sushi is cheap and fun — grab what looks good!

food.name: Takoyaki
food.description: Octopus-filled batter balls topped with sauce, mayo, and bonito flakes. Hot and addictive.

food.name: Okonomiyaki
food.description: Savory Japanese pancake with cabbage, meat/seafood, and toppings. Cooked on a hot plate at your table.

food.name: Matcha Desserts
food.description: Green tea flavored everything — soft serve, parfaits, lattes, and traditional wagashi sweets.

food.name: Gyoza
food.description: Pan-fried dumplings filled with pork and garlic. Best with soy sauce, vinegar, and chili oil.
